mainTopic: רב נחמן on מתנת שכיב מרע: its rabbinic source, its Torah-level strength, and what a dying person can give
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: knowing the year's weather in advance helps the כהן גדול direct his תפילה. Then the גמרא turns to מתנת שכיב מרע. רבא quotes רב נחמן that this gift works only מדרבנן, so that the dying man won't become upset. The גמרא challenges this from another ruling of רב נחמן. There, שמואל agrees that if a creditor gave a שטר חוב as a deathbed gift, his heir cannot cancel the debt, which seems to assume the gift is Torah-level. The answer is that חכמים gave this rabbinic gift the full strength of a Torah law. Next, רב נחמן rules that a שכיב מרע cannot give only the right to live in a house or eat a tree's fruit. He must give the house or tree itself. The גמרא infers that a dying person can give only what a healthy person can give. It then begins to challenge this with another statement of רב נחמן, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the weather forecast matters: the כהן גדול's prayer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier question. Knowing the coming year's weather matters for the תפילה of the כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The practical difference is] for the prayer of the כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a question asked just before this section: what practical difference does it make to know in advance what the year's weather will be? The answer is that it shapes the כהן גדול's prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think a weather forecast has no practical use. The answer gives it one: the כהן גדול can direct his prayer according to what the year needs. This closes the earlier topic before the גמרא moves on.

phrases.english: For the prayer of the High Priest.
phrases.notes: This answers the question just before this line: what difference does knowing the year's weather make?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a question-and-answer exchange that began before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference does knowing the year's weather make?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It lets the כהן גדול direct his prayer to fit the year's needs.

steps.title: רב נחמן: a deathbed gift works only by rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes רב נחמן: מתנת שכיב מרע is valid only מדרבנן, so that the dying man does not become distressed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: the gift of a שכיב מרע is only a rabbinic law. It was made so that his mind will not become upset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main topic of deathbed gifts. רבא reports רב נחמן's view that such a gift works only because חכמים said so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a gift needs a קנין (act of acquisition), but a שכיב מרע's spoken words are enough. רב נחמן says this power comes from חכמים, not the Torah. The reason is that if a dying man saw his wishes ignored, he could fall into despair and his condition could get worse.

keyTerms.meaning: the gift of a person on his deathbed
his mind will become upset or confused

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying a deathbed gift is weak or optional. He is only saying where its power comes from: חכמים, not a פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether a law is from the Torah or from חכמים can change how strong it is in practice. The next steps test exactly this.

phrases.english: And Rava said in the name of Rav Nachman:
The gift of a person on his deathbed
phrases.notes: He means it works through words alone, without the usual act of acquiring.

phrases.english: is merely by rabbinic law,
lest his mind become upset on him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the weather topic and returns to the main topic of deathbed gifts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מתנת שכיב מרע is valid only by rabbinic law, to keep the dying man from despair.

steps.title: Challenge from רב נחמן's ruling on a forgiven loan document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב נחמן really said this. Elsewhere he said that if a creditor gives a שטר חוב as a deathbed gift, the heir cannot forgive the debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רב נחמן really say this? But רב נחמן said: שמואל holds that if someone sells a loan document to another and then forgives the debt, it is forgiven, and even an heir can forgive it. Still, שמואל agrees that if he gave it as a deathbed gift, it cannot be forgiven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב נחמן's statement by quoting another ruling of his that seems to point the other way. This step brings in the source; the next step explains why it is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says that when a שטר חוב is sold, the original lender, and even his heir, can still cancel the debt. רב נחמן reports that שמואל himself agrees this does not apply when the document was given as a מתנת שכיב מרע: then the heir cannot cancel it. This means the deathbed gift is treated as stronger than an ordinary sale.

keyTerms.meaning: and did he really say? (opens a challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: In a regular sale of a שטר חוב, the seller can still cancel the debt, because the borrower's debt is to him. That is why the deathbed-gift exception stands out.

phrases.english: And did Rav Nachman really say this?!
But didn't Rav Nachman say:
Even though Shmuel said:
One who sells a loan document to his fellow,
and then went back and forgave it, it is forgiven;
and even an heir can forgive it;
phrases.notes: The seller's heir also has the power to cancel the debt.

phrases.english: Shmuel agrees that if he gave it
as the gift of a person on his deathbed,
that he cannot forgive it.
phrases.notes: The giver has died, so 'he' here is the heir, who now cannot cancel the debt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 2 using a different statement from the same אמורא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim in step 2 that מתנת שכיב מרע is only rabbinic.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His other ruling makes a deathbed gift so strong that the heir cannot cancel it, which seems to fit a Torah-level gift.

steps.title: Spelling out the contradiction: Torah law versus rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: If the deathbed gift is Torah law, it makes sense that the heir cannot cancel the debt. If it is only rabbinic, why can't he?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if you say it is Torah law: that is why he cannot forgive. But if you say it is rabbinic, why can't he forgive?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains exactly why the source in step 3 is a problem for רב נחמן's statement in step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Torah-level gift could fully transfer the debt, leaving the heir nothing to cancel. A merely rabbinic gift seems too weak to override the heir's Torah-level power to forgive. So the ruling from step 3 seems to require that the gift be דאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: it makes sense if you say

phrases.english: It makes sense if you say it is by Torah law,
because of that he cannot forgive.
But if you say it is by rabbinic law,
why can he not forgive?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge from step 3 by explaining why that source contradicts step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rabbinic status of מתנת שכיב מרע (step 2).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbinic gift should not be strong enough to block the heir's power to forgive; only a Torah-level gift explains it.

steps.title: Answer: חכמים gave it the strength of Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The deathbed gift is not from the Torah, but חכמים made it as strong as a Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not from the Torah, but they made it like Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Both of רב נחמן's statements can be true together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source of the deathbed gift is rabbinic, just as רב נחמן said in step 2. But חכמים gave it full Torah-level force, so it really transfers the debt and the heir cannot cancel it. The contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not from the Torah
like a Torah law, with the same force

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן: מתנת שכיב מרע comes from חכמים, so the dying man won't despair. But חכמים gave it the full strength of Torah law, so even a שטר חוב given this way cannot be canceled by the heir.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a key idea: a rabbinic law can be given the same practical power as a Torah law. Its source and its strength are two separate questions.

phrases.english: It is not of Torah law,
but they made it like Torah law.
phrases.notes: 'They' are חכמים, who gave this gift full Torah-level strength.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה וַעֲשָׂאוּהָ כְּשֶׁל תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in steps 3 and 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes between the source of a law and the strength given to it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A rabbinic gift is too weak to stop the heir from forgiving the debt.
steps.terutzMaskana: Though rabbinic in origin, חכמים gave the deathbed gift Torah-level force, so the heir cannot cancel the debt.

steps.title: A deathbed person cannot give just the right to live in a house or eat fruit
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes רב נחמן: a שכיב מרע who gives only the use of a house or the fruit of a tree has said nothing. He must give the house or tree itself, and then the person may live there or eat the fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: If a dying person says 'So-and-so shall live in this house' or 'So-and-so shall eat the fruit of this palm tree,' he has not said anything. It only works if he says 'Give this house to so-and-so and let him live in it' or 'Give this palm tree to so-and-so and let him eat its fruit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב נחמן about the exact wording a dying person must use when giving a gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Living in a house or eating fruit that has not grown yet is only a right to use something. It is not a physical thing that can be handed over. So the dying man must give the object itself, the house or the tree, and the use then comes along with it.

keyTerms.meaning: He has not said anything; his words have no legal effect
Give! (a command to the people around him)

phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Nachman said:
A person on his deathbed who said:
"So-and-so shall live in this house,"
or "So-and-so shall eat the fruit of this palm tree":
he has not said anything,
phrases.notes: Living somewhere or eating future fruit is only a right to use. You can't hand that over by itself, so his words don't work.

phrases.english: until he says:
"Give this house to so-and-so and let him live in it,"
or "Give this palm tree to so-and-so and let him eat its fruit."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: שְׁכִיב מְרַע שֶׁאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement from רבא in רב נחמן's name about deathbed gifts, following the earlier discussion of מתנת שכיב מרע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שכיב מרע cannot give only the right to live in a house or eat a tree's fruit. He must give the house or tree itself.

steps.title: Does a dying person's gift work only where a healthy person's would?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws a conclusion from רב נחמן's ruling: a שכיב מרע can give only what a healthy person can give. It then starts to quote a different statement of רב נחמן that seems to go against this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean רב נחמן holds that whatever works for a healthy person works for a dying person, and whatever does not work for a healthy person does not work for a dying person? But didn't רבא say in the name of רב נחמן:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls a general rule out of the last ruling. Then it gets ready to challenge that rule with another quote from רב נחמן, which comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A healthy person cannot give a bare right of use, and רב נחמן ruled that a dying person cannot either. That suggests the dying person's gift is no stronger than a healthy person's gift. The words 'וְהָא אָמַר' tell us that another statement of רב נחמן is about to contradict this.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say? (the גמרא draws a conclusion, usually so it can question it)
It works (exists) / it does not work (does not exist)
But isn't it so that...? (opens a challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop at the question mark. The real challenge is the quote that starts with 'וְהָא אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן', and that quote continues right after this.

phrases.english: Is this to say that Rav Nachman holds
that something which works for a healthy person
works for a person on his deathbed,
and something that does not work for a healthy person
does not work for a person on his deathbed?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: But didn't Rava say that Rav Nachman said:

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּסָבַר רַב נַחְמָן מִילְּתָא דְּאִיתָא בְּבָרִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule from step 6 and starts to challenge it with another statement of רב נחמן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from step 6 that a שכיב מרע can give only what a בריא can give.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another statement of רב נחמן, quoted next, seems to let a dying person give something a healthy person cannot. That would contradict the rule drawn from step 6.
